question: (1) The 2026 federal deposit schedule for withheld income tax and both shares of Social Security and Medicare: the monthly versus semiweekly lookback rule, the next-day rule, the small-employer annual and quarterly options, and the penalty for a late deposit. (2) FUTA: how the up-to-5.4% credit depends on state unemployment contributions, and which states are credit-reduction states for 2026. (3) State unemployment insurance for each state and D.C.: the 2026 taxable wage base and the new-employer rate. Mark each figure with its source; UNKNOWN where not verified.

title: When an employer must pay its payroll taxes, and what unemployment tax it owes
usableAnswer: The deposit rules with dates and penalty percentages; the FUTA credit rule and 2026 credit-reduction states; one row per state with UI wage base and new-employer rate, each cited.
whyItMatters: The game now records the employer's share of Social Security and Medicare on every paycheck but cannot say when it is due, so an employer's balance is owed with no due date and can never become late. FUTA and state unemployment tax are recorded as UNKNOWN.
